knowledge:
- key_parameters: strata=vsn2 parameter to choose different offset and scaling factors for different groups (strata) of rows (e.g., print-tip groups or PCR plates) ;; calib=vsn2 parameter to control calibration; set to "none" to apply global variance stabilization without column- or row-specific calibration ;; backgroundsubtract=justvsn parameter for RGList objects; if TRUE, subtracts local background estimates in the Rb and Gb slots ;; lts.quantile=vsn2 parameter controlling the robustness (fraction of data used for least trimmed sum of squares regression, default 0.9, allows 10% outliers) ;; reference=vsn2 parameter to normalize new test arrays against an existing reference vsn fit object
- alternatives: rma=from the affy package, used for Affymetrix genechip preprocessing; vsnrma is a wrapper combining VSN and RMA summarisation, which controls variance at low intensities more strongly than rma ;; normalizeQuantiles=from the limma package, can be used for quantile normalization prior to running VSN with calib="none" ;; loess=non-linear regression on A-values to force the center of the M distribution to 0; VSN with strata is preferred if the bias is not strongly confounded with A
- when_to_use: Appropriate for preprocessing microarray intensity data (two-color cDNA arrays, single-color arrays, Affymetrix genechips) or similar high-throughput intensity data to stabilize variance (making variance independent of the mean) and calibrate systematic experimental factors.
- pitfalls: Numerical instability/convergence errors (e.g., "L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'") can occur due to preprocessing bugs, poor data quality, incompatible measurements, or unsuitable noise characteristics ;; Subtracting local background estimates can increase random noise if there is no actual local spatial gradient or variability ;; VSN only addresses variance dependence on mean intensity; other determinants of variance (technical, sample-inherent, gene-inherent) require other models ;; VSN cannot simultaneously calibrate and transform data from different manufacturing batches (batch effects).

workflows.name: standard_microarray_normalization
workflows.intent: Calibrate and variance-stabilize microarray intensity data from ExpressionSet or matrix objects.
workflows.stages:
1. Run one-step normalization with justvsn
2. Alternatively, run two-step normalization by fitting parameters with vsn2 and applying them with predict
3. Assess variance stabilization using meanSdPlot
4. Perform spike-in normalization or normalization without calibration if required
workflows.code:
xnorm = justvsn(kidney)
M = exprs(xnorm)[,1] - exprs(xnorm)[,2]
fit = vsn2(kidney)
ynorm = predict(fit, kidney)
meanSdPlot(xnorm, ranks = TRUE)
meanSdPlot(xnorm, ranks = FALSE)
spfit = vsn2(kidney[spikeins,], lts.quantile=1)
nkid = predict(spfit, newdata=kidney)
lym_qvsn = vsn2(lym_q, calib="none")

workflows.name: affymetrix_genechip_normalization
workflows.intent: Preprocess Affymetrix genechip data using the RMA method with VSN background correction, normalization, and transformation.
input: Dilution (AffyBatch object containing raw Affymetrix intensity data)
workflows.stages: 1. Run vsnrma to perform background correction, between-array normalization, transformation, and summarization.

workflows.name: rglist_normalization
workflows.intent: Normalize and transform two-color microarray data stored in an RGList object.
input: lymRG (RGList object containing red and green intensities)
lymRGwbg (RGList object containing red and green intensities with background estimates)
workflows.stages: 1. Run justvsn on the RGList object (optionally with background subtraction or strata).
workflows.code:
lymNCS = justvsn(lymRG)
lymESwbg = justvsn(lymRGwbg[, 1:3], backgroundsubtract=TRUE)
EconStr = justvsn(lymRG[, 1], strata = arrayGeometry$pin)

workflows.name: reference_normalization
workflows.intent: Normalize new test arrays against an existing reference dataset without changing the reference parameters.
input: lymphoma (ExpressionSet containing reference and new test arrays)
workflows.stages:
1. Fit the VSN model on the reference arrays using vsn2.
2. Fit the VSN model on the new arrays using vsn2 with the reference parameter.
workflows.code:
ref = vsn2(lymphoma[, ismp[1:7]])
f8 = vsn2(lymphoma[, ismp[8]], reference = ref)
fall = vsn2(lymphoma[, ismp])
